title: IT Administrator & HR Executive
description:
**About the Role:**

We are an established landscape design, contracting, and civil execution firm handling comprehensive commercial, plotted development, and landscape turnkey projects.

We are seeking a proactive **IT Administrator cum HR Executive** to manage our core office IT infrastructure and people operations. In this dual role, you will ensure our design and project management workstations, drafting software, and communication tools run seamlessly, while managing site/office staff onboarding, daily attendance tracking, asset management, and general HR administrative workflows.

**Key Responsibilities:1. IT Administration & Technical Infrastructure:**

* Configure, maintain, and troubleshoot office workstations, laptops, operating systems (Windows), and peripheral hardware (large-format plotters, printers, network scanners).
* Manage software installation, workstation performance, and license coordination for drafting, 3D design, and office tools (e.g., CAD software, rendering tools, office suites).
* Maintain office networking, Wi-Fi connectivity, switches, routers, and resolve internet downtime with local ISPs promptly.
* Administer business email accounts (Google Workspace / Microsoft 365), internal portals/ERP systems, user access permissions, and shared project drives.
* Manage regular data backups of site drawings, CAD files, project BOQs, and estimates; ensure endpoint security across all machines.

**2. HR & Workforce Operations:**

* Coordinate recruitment for office technical staff (landscape architects, 3D visualizers, quantity surveyors, CAD draftsmen) and on-site execution teams (site engineers, supervisors).
* Manage end-to-end employee onboarding: document collection, ID verification, offer letters, asset allocation, and system provisioning.
* Track daily attendance and leave management across both office staff and site execution teams (via biometric portals, mobile apps, or attendance registers).
* Prepare monthly attendance summaries and payroll inputs for timely salary processing.
* Maintain company asset tracking records (laptops, site tablets/phones, measuring equipment, office keys).
* Coordinate basic HR administrative policies, employee inquiries, grievance resolution, and statutory compliance documentation.

Pay: ₹10,000.00 - ₹38,000.00 per month

Work Location: In person

title: Head (Senior Manager) - Industrial Relations
description:
### **About the Team**

You will join the Security & Investigations team within Fulfilment & Experience (F&E) at Meesho. F&E is the operational and technological backbone powering India's cost-efficient, reliable and scalable e-commerce network, serving 100M+ monthly active users. From enabling Valmo's distributed logistics network to building scalable fulfilment and experience platforms, F&E operates at the intersection of technology, operations and network innovation.

Within F&E, the Security & Investigations team safeguards the integrity and resilience of this network. The team investigates shipment loss, pilferage, fraud and misconduct, oversees physical security across operating sites, and coordinates with law enforcement and other stakeholders where required. Working closely with Operations, HR, Legal and logistics partners, the team helps keep the network secure, compliant and resilient.

### **About the Role**

Valmo's operating network is powered by a large and diverse workforce spanning sort centres, hubs and last-mile operations. A significant portion of this workforce is engaged through logistics partners and other workforce arrangements, creating a complex industrial-relations environment across multiple locations and states.

As Head – Industrial Relations, you will own the Industrial Relations (IR) charter for the operating network, within the Security & Investigations function, and work closely with HR, Legal, Operations and partner leadership. Your mandate will be to build a stable, compliant and scalable workforce-relations framework that prevents avoidable disputes, enables fair and timely resolution of workforce issues, and provides strong governance when matters escalate.

The role combines strategic IR leadership with significant field engagement. You will build early-warning mechanisms, manage worker and union relationships, oversee dispute and disciplinary processes, strengthen partner workforce compliance, engage with labour authorities, and create playbooks and governance mechanisms that can scale with the network.

### **What You Will Do**

**Own IR strategy and governance.** Build and continuously evolve a national IR framework covering workforce relations, grievance management, dispute prevention, statutory compliance, worker/union engagement, escalation and resolution.

**Build workforce intelligence and early-warning mechanisms.** Track workforce sentiment, grievances, absenteeism, wage-related concerns, shift and working-condition issues, emerging worker representation or union activity, and other indicators of potential disruption across the network.

**Prevent and manage industrial disputes.** Develop structured approaches to prevent disputes and lead the response to strikes, work stoppages, protests, gheraos and other workforce disruptions. Engage with worker representatives and union leaders and coordinate with Operations, HR, Legal, partners, local administration, labour authorities and law enforcement, as appropriate.

**Bring IR rigour to investigations.** Partner with Security & Investigations, HR and Legal on cases involving employees or partner workers, including theft, fraud, misconduct and policy violations. Ensure due process, appropriate documentation and legally sound decision-making.

**Govern disciplinary processes.** Oversee show-cause notices, domestic enquiries and disciplinary actions, ensuring that processes are fair, consistent, timely and legally defensible under applicable law, standing orders and organisational policy.

**Drive partner workforce compliance.** Establish and monitor governance over logistics partners covering contract labour requirements, wage and benefits compliance, statutory registrations, working hours, worker documentation, grievance mechanisms and other applicable labour requirements. Drive timely corrective action and escalation where gaps are identified.

**Own government and authority engagement.** Build effective working relationships with labour departments, labour commissioners, conciliation officers and other relevant government authorities. Represent the organisation in inspections, conciliation proceedings and hearings, in partnership with Legal, and coordinate with Security on matters requiring law-enforcement engagement.

**Build effective grievance and escalation channels.** Design and strengthen mechanisms such as worker helplines, site-level committees, grievance forums and escalation paths so that workforce concerns are surfaced and resolved before they become formal disputes.

**Create scalable IR playbooks and capability.** Develop SOPs, policies, escalation matrices and response playbooks for dispute management, investigation-linked disciplinary action, partner workforce issues and authority engagement. Train site leaders, partner supervisors, HR teams and security personnel on relevant IR practices and labour-law basics.

**Build IR analytics and leadership reporting.** Establish dashboards and regular reviews covering incidents, disputes, grievances, compliance health, partner risks, resolution timelines, repeat issues and emerging trends. Translate these into clear insights and actions for senior leadership.

**Strengthen cross-functional governance.** Establish clear interfaces between IR, HR, Legal, Operations, Security & Investigations and partner leadership, including decision rights, escalation threshold

### **What You Will Need**

* 8–15 years of experience in industrial relations, employee relations, labour relations or labour-law compliance, preferably in large, distributed workforce environments.
* Experience in logistics, e-commerce, manufacturing, warehousing, retail, infrastructure or other large blue-collar and/or contract-workforce environments is strongly preferred.
* Deep working knowledge of applicable Indian labour and employment laws, including the Labour Codes and associated rules/notifications, contract labour requirements, industrial disputes, standing orders and relevant state-specific requirements.
* Practical experience applying labour law and IR principles on the ground across multiple sites and, ideally, multiple states.
* Proven experience handling industrial disputes, worker grievances, union/worker representative engagement, negotiations, strikes or work stoppages.
* Experience conducting or overseeing domestic enquiries and disciplinary proceedings, with a strong understanding of how employee investigations intersect with employment law and due process.
* Experience managing contract labour or partner workforce compliance, including audits, statutory requirements, wage-related compliance and remediation.
* Strong ability to engage with labour authorities, conciliation officers and other government stakeholders, preferably with experience representing an organisation in formal proceedings.
* Strong negotiation, conflict-resolution and stakeholder-management skills, with the ability to remain calm, credible and objective in high-pressure situations.
* Ability to work effectively across HR, Legal, Operations, Security & Investigations and external partners, with sound judgement on ownership, escalation and confidentiality.
* Strong communication skills in English and Hindi. Proficiency in one or more regional languages is an advantage, particularly for workforce-heavy operating regions.
* Strong analytical and problem-solving ability, including the ability to use workforce and incident data to identify patterns, risks and preventive actions.
* Willingness to travel extensively across operating locations and respond to sensitive on-ground situations at short notice.
* High integrity, discretion and maturity, with the ability to handle confidential matters and decisions that can materially affect employees and workers.
* A degree in law, HR, labour welfare, social work or a related discipline (LLB, MSW, MBA-HR or equivalent) is preferred.

**Role Characteristics**

* National scope with significant field engagement across the operating network.
* High level of cross-functional and external stakeholder interaction.
* Combination of strategic programme ownership, operational problem-solving and on-ground dispute management.
* Requires sound judgement, neutrality, confidentiality and the ability to balance business continuity with fair and compliant workforce practices.

You will also act as a trusted advisor to Sales and clients, using market insight and data to shape realistic requirements, rates and timelines.

**Key responsibilities**

**Delivery ownership**

* Own monthly and quarterly hiring targets (selections and joiners) for the accounts in scope.

* Track every requirement from intake to joining, and step in early when a role stalls, a candidate disengages or an offer is at risk.

**Stakeholder management**

* Lead intake and calibration discussions so every role has a clear brief, a realistic budget and an agreed interview process before sourcing starts.
* Agree feedback timelines with Sales and clients, and follow up with data when they slip.

**People leadership**

* Lead, coach and manage team leads and recruiters against clear weekly productivity goals.

**Quality and candidate experience**

* Make sure every candidate receives timely updates and a clear outcome.

* Work closely with the central sourcing team on role allocation, handovers and turnaround time.

**Job Title:** Lead Specialist, HR Operations

**Description:** This role aligns with industry titles such as Vendor Management Systems (VMS) Program Manager, MSP Program Manager, VMS product Manager or Beeline VMS Administrator

**The Role**

We are the HR Product Owner team. We decide what gets built in Oracle and ServiceNow, in what order, and why. The HR community brings us their problems and their ideas, and we make sure they get into the system, get prioritised, and get tested before they reach anyone. Our colleagues never need to go to the technology teams directly. That is our job.

Each of us owns a domain end to end: onboarding and offboarding journeys, leave and absence, talent management, benefits and vendor management. This role adds the one domain we are missing.

As Program Manager and PO for Contingent Workforce, you will own the contingent worker journey as a product, from the moment someone is sourced, through onboarding, extensions and role changes, to the day they leave and their access is closed cleanly. Hire to retire, with one owner.

Today that journey runs across a vendor management system, Oracle Fusion, ServiceNow and our identity platforms, with different teams owning different pieces and nobody holding the whole thread. A working prototype already exists: a single conversational front door where a hiring manager gives the information once and the systems do the rest, with no tickets raised at all. Your job is to take that from a promising prototype to a permanent service, and to extend it across the full lifecycle.

This is not a role about keeping a system running. You will bring a process architect mindset to simplify genuine complexity, working with shared services, global HR systems and emerging technologies such as robotic process automation and artificial intelligence, so that the contingent worker experience becomes something we design rather than something that happens.

**What You'll Own**

Own the contingent worker journey end to end as a product, with a clear roadmap, prioritised increments and measurable outcomes.

Act as business owner of our vendor management system (Beeline), covering configuration, supplier onboarding, rate card structures, worker classification and reporting.

Manage the relationship with the vendor management system provider and with staffing suppliers, holding both to agreed service levels.

Map the journey across Talent Acquisition, Procurement, Finance, IT, Security, and the country teams, then redesign it rather than simply document it.

Identify where policy rather than technology is the real blocker, and build the case to change it.

Maintain the role-based profile model so that access and equipment are provisioned automatically for standard roles, and manually only for genuine exceptions.

Translate what you learn into what gets built in Oracle and ServiceNow, and see it through to testing and adoption.

Work alongside the Global Process Owner for Hire-to-Onboard, and with the teams building provisioning for permanent employees, so we converge on one pattern rather than several.

Bring security, compliance and audit in early, not at the point of go-live.

Define and track what good looks like: time from source to day one, day one readiness, tickets raised per worker, and satisfaction of both the worker and the hiring manager.

**About You**

Five to eight years of experience in contingent workforce programmes, managed service provider models, or HR operations with direct contingent workforce responsibility.

Hands-on ownership of a vendor management system such as Beeline or SAP Fieldglass, including configuration, supplier management and reporting. Experience as an end user alone is not enough for this role.

A process architect mindset: you can map a cross-functional journey, find where the time and the friction actually sit, and simplify it.

Comfort with data. You build the measurement case yourself rather than waiting for a report.

Proven success working in a matrix environment, influencing across functions without direct authority.

Curiosity and openness to innovation, including robotic process automation, artificial intelligence and agent-based workflows.

Clear written communication. Much of this role is making a complex journey understandable to people who own only one part of it.

Working knowledge of Oracle Fusion, ServiceNow and identity platforms such as Microsoft Entra is an advantage.

Understanding of contingent worker classification and compliance requirements across multiple countries is an advantage.

**What You'll Get**

You will own a journey that thousands of people at Pearson experience, and you will own it properly: the system, the process, the suppliers and the roadmap. Few roles at this level give you that much of a canvas.

You will also arrive at the right moment. The problem is already evidenced, a prototype already works, and there is executive attention on the outcome. What is missing is a single owner to turn it into something permanent and scale it.

As the world's leading learning company, Pearson is transforming how people learn, work and grow. You will be based in India and working globally, with hybrid and flexible working, and with a team of product owners around you who are solving the same kind of problem in their own domains.

**Ready to make an Impact?**

Apply now and help shape what’s next.

At Pearson, our purpose is simple: to help people realize the life they imagine through learning. We believe that every learning opportunity is a chance for a personal breakthrough. We are the world's lifelong learning company. For us, learning isn't just what we do. It's who we are. To learn more: We are Pearson.

Signeasy began 16 years ago with a simple idea: signing should be easy. That idea helped the world go paperless. But signatures were only the beginning.

2025 changed everything. While others continued to treat contracts as paperwork, we began turning them into living, searchable, and intelligent systems of record.
